title: Tech Note: Simplifying and Optimizing HTML Construction
author: David Adams

historical_commentary.text: Written in March 1996 when using 4D to generate HTML (as a CGI processor or emerging built-in web server) was novel, this note's core idea — storing HTML templates as data records with placeholder tokens and using fast string replacement instead of concatenating markup in code — is a timeless templating pattern still recognizable in modern templating engines. However, the specific implementation (Replace string, parameter indirection with ${n}, manually cached arrays) is tied to the pre-Method/pre-ORDA 4D procedural language and predates 4D's built-in web server, WebAdmin, and any modern templating or REST-based approach.
related_updates: 4D gained a genuine built-in Web Server and 4D Internet Commands plugin in the years after this note (~1997-1998), replacing ad hoc CGI-style HTML generation
Modern 4D web development typically uses ORDA/REST APIs with front-end JS frameworks rendering HTML/JSON client-side, rather than server-side string templating in 4D code
Procedures were renamed Methods starting with 4D v6 (1997), and parameter/array handling has evolved substantially with object notation and collections
